title: Frontier-flagship LLM pricing re-anchors to the $10/$50 premium band by Q3 2026
body: Anthropic's June 9 launch of Claude Fable 5 as a paid Mythos-class flagship priced at $10 per million input and $50 per million output tokens - double the Opus 4.8 rate - sets a new premium ceiling for generally available frontier models and pairs it with a hard monetization cliff, with free Pro/Max/Team/Enterprise access ending June 22 before usage-credit gating begins. The prediction is that this re-anchors flagship-tier economics across the market: by Q3 2026 at least one competing lab prices or repositions its own top model at or above the roughly $10-input / $50-output band Fable established, and Anthropic's post-June-22 credit-metered access becomes the reference commercial shape for the highest-capability tier. The signal is a deliberate move away from a single uniformly priced public frontier toward a stratified, premium-gated top tier, which gives rivals cover to lift their own flagship list prices rather than compete them down even as a Broadcom-led pullback presses on AI-capex sentiment.

reasoning.because: Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5 June 9 at $10/$50 per M tokens, double Opus; free tier ends June 22
reasoning.given: a tiered premium-flagship launch lets rival labs lift top-model prices under cover, not discount
reasoning.so_that: at least one competing lab prices or repositions its flagship at or above the ~$10-input / $50-output band Fable set
reasoning.landing: by Q3 2026; >=1 rival flagship-pricing move plus credit-gated Fable access live
reasoning.plain_language: Anthropic's newest AI costs twice as much as its last, giving rivals an excuse to raise their own top prices too.

summary: Anthropic's June 9 Claude Fable 5 launch set a premium $10/$50-per-million-token flagship ceiling, double Opus, with free access ending June 22. Expect flagship LLM pricing to re-anchor upward: by Q3 2026 at least one rival lab prices its top model at or above that band.
